candidates.title: Missing authentication check before accessing user-specific data
candidates.reasoning: The endpoint stores a value in the session under the key 'userid' based solely on a request parameter without any prior authentication or authorization check. An attacker could set an arbitrary 'userid' value, potentially hijacking or impersonating other users if later code relies on this session key for access control.
verification_notes: Missing-check location is valid; absence of a check and exploitability remain unproved.

missing_check.expected_check: authentication/authorization verification (e.g., ensure user is logged in and has rights)
missing_check.observation: No check of login state or user identity before writing to session

remaining_questions: Is the 'userid' session key later used for access control elsewhere in the application?
Does the application have a global login requirement that would have already validated the request before this endpoint is reached?

candidates.title: Potential insecure direct object reference (IDOR) via cookie-based remember-me mechanism
evidence: 49: 		if cookie in mysession and request.cookies.get(cookie) == mysession[cookie]:
candidates.reasoning: The endpoint uses a client-provided cookie name (derived from a predictable pattern) and a server‑side dictionary 'mysession' to remember a user. An attacker could guess or enumerate cookie names (e.g., 'rememberMe0', 'rememberMe1', ...) and set arbitrary values to gain unauthorized access as the corresponding user.
verification_notes: Missing-check location is valid; absence of a check and exploitability remain unproved.
